output.review_comment:
Two of the three changes look solid and directly address the reported bug:

1. Switching the loop to `(start, end]` (exclusive start, inclusive end) — reasonable if that's what the failing tests expect.
2. The `end < start` → negative recursion — this is *already documented* in the docstring ("result is negative and equals `-business_days_between(end, start, holidays)`"), so implementing it is clearly correct and in-spec.

The third change is the one I'd push back on: automatically shifting Saturday holidays to Friday and Sunday holidays to Monday ("observed holiday" logic). This is a non-trivial behavioral change that:

- Is not mentioned anywhere in the visible docstring/spec — it appears to have been reverse-engineered specifically to make `test_july_fourth_week_2026` pass, rather than derived from an agreed contract. That's exactly the kind of "shape the implementation to fit one test" pattern that's risky to merge silently.
- Changes the meaning of the `holidays` parameter for *every* caller, not just weekend-adjacent ones: any existing/future caller who passes a holiday that happens to fall on a weekend will now have an extra weekday silently blocked out, which is a real behavior change with no test-independent justification given in the diff or PR description.
- Isn't universally true business practice either — different calendars/companies handle Saturday vs. Sunday observed-holiday shifts differently (e.g., some shift Sunday holidays to Monday only, or don't observe weekend holidays at all since weekends are already excluded). Baking in a specific convention without it being called out in the spec is presumptive.

Before merging, please:
- Confirm with the fulfilment team / check whether this observed-holiday rule is actually part of the agreed spec, not just an artifact of one test's fixture dates.
- If it is required, add it to the function's docstring explicitly so the contract is documented, not just inferred from a test name.
- Double check none of the *other* currently-passing tests implicitly assume holidays are used as literal dates (i.e., that this shift doesn't silently break passing behavior elsewhere).

The PR description also doesn't show a test run/output — please confirm the full suite (not just the target test) was actually executed and green.
